summary: Shows running the shell module ad hoc and warns about local shell quoting: single quotes pass the variable to the remote host, while double quotes expand it on the control machine.
questions: Why does my ad hoc shell command print the variable value from my laptop instead of the remote host?
Should I use single or double quotes around ad hoc shell arguments?
How do I run a shell command with environment variables on remote hosts ad hoc?

answer_card.title: Quoting in ad hoc shell commands
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
ansible raleigh -m ansible.builtin.shell -a 'echo $TERM'
```
Use **single quotes** so your local shell doesn't expand the variable. With double quotes, `$TERM` is evaluated on the control machine before Ansible sees it.
